svg.title: Fabric Mirroring from Source to OneLake
svg.desc: A flow diagram showing how database mirroring creates an initial baseline snapshot, continuously replicates change data feeds without ETL, materializes Delta tables in OneLake, and serves analytical consumers.
svg.text: Fabric Database Mirroring: Source to OneLake Delta Replica
Zero-ETL Ingestion · Baseline Snapshot · Continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) · Direct Lake Analytics

g.title: Operational source — A supported database remains the transactional system of record.
g.text: Continuous write workloads remain untouched without analytical query contention
• 0 custom integration scripts or maintenance of third-party ETL connector software
• User selects individual tables or mirrors whole database schemas selectively
• Primary key required on replicated tables for deterministic row identity.
• Source system transaction log retention must accommodate planned sync windows.
• Network connectivity verified via Azure Service Endpoints or Managed Private Endpoints.

g.title: Initial snapshot — Mirroring establishes a baseline before ongoing changes are meaningful.
g.text: One-time historical extraction establishing the replicated baseline
• Automatic batching avoids locking production tables during initial bulk copy
• Multi-terabyte databases partition baseline across parallel copy streams
• Downstream Direct Lake queries should wait until status reaches "Running".
• Once baseline is committed, replication switches automatically to streaming CDC.

g.title: Managed change replication — Fabric continuously applies source changes without user-authored ETL.
g.text: Continuous serverless change synchronization without ETL compute overhead
• Continuously polls source transaction log / change feed using LSN pointers
• Stages incremental change files (Inserts, Updates, Deletes) into landing zone
• Automatically merges changes into Delta Lake target with zero manual MERGE SQL
• Near-real-time synchronization latency typically measured in seconds
• Add column in source ➔ Automatically replicates into Delta schema seamlessly.
• Incompatible schema alterations trigger table-level pause with explicit error message.
• Auto-managed backoff & retry prevents connection storms during source maintenance.
Key Advantage: Free serverless data movement compute — 0 CU charge for ingestion!

g.title: OneLake Delta replica — Replicated data is stored as Delta away from transaction processing.
g.text: Open standard Delta Parquet format stored in tenant's single logical OneLake
• Persisted as open-source Delta Lake tables with full `_delta_log/` history
• Automatic write-time V-Order optimization accelerates VertiPaq/Direct Lake reads
• Decoupled storage allows analytical queries to scale independently of OLTP source
• Stored inside Mirrored Database item in target Fabric workspace
• Automatic compaction merges small delta files to maintain optimal read performance.
• Retention & Vacuum policies purge expired transaction logs per governance settings.
• Read-only replica: DDL/DML mutations must happen at authoritative source database.
Single Copy Guarantee: Shared across all Fabric engines with 0 duplication.

g.title: Analytical consumers — SQL, Direct Lake, Spark, and other workloads read the replica.
g.text: Instant queryability across BI, warehousing, and data engineering experiences
• Reflects source DB updates in seconds
• Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoint
• Direct read via delta table path
• Trains ML models on fresh data
Mirroring eliminates fragile batch ETL jobs for operational reporting. Because data lands as standard Delta Lake in OneLake,
Power BI dashboards query the replica with sub-second Direct Lake speed without impacting transactional OLTP throughput.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Database Mirroring Specs.
